1	/**
2	 * Folding a stream of events into a map that is being built.
3	 *
4	 * One pure function from (state, event) to state. It draws no pixels, makes no
5	 * requests, and **does no arithmetic**: every number it holds is a field it was
6	 * handed. Counting the rows in a list it holds is not arithmetic on the map's
7	 * numbers, and neither is asking whether a list is empty.
8	 *
9	 * Three rules shape everything below.
10	 *
11	 * **The likelihoods replace the map wholesale.** Until they arrive, the world
12	 * here is the browser's drawing of the proposals it has watched go past — the
13	 * claims, the arrows, and an absence with its reason in every likelihood slot.
14	 * When the engine's own world arrives it *is* the world, and the drawing is
15	 * thrown away rather than merged into. A browser keeping its own version beside
16	 * the engine's would be a second source of truth, and two sources of truth
17	 * disagree.
18	 *
19	 * **Nothing here mints an identifier.** A claim's identifier is minted by the
20	 * engine and arrives on the event. The one name this file makes is a reserved
21	 * rectangle's, it names a rectangle rather than a claim, and it is thrown away
22	 * the moment that claim stops being open.
23	 *
24	 * **A wire is drawn only when both of its ends exist.** In practice the engine
25	 * makes that true by construction — a claim and its incoming arrows arrive in one
26	 * event — and this file does not rely on it. An arrow whose two ends are not both
27	 * on the map is held and drawn the moment the second one arrives. A wire with one
28	 * end nowhere is a picture of something that is not true.
29	 *
30	 * **And one event is folded into none of that** *(added 2026-09-22, Kent's R44
31	 * and R47)*. `activity` — what the model is doing inside a call that has not
32	 * come back — changes one field, `activity`, and nothing else: not the map, not
33	 * the rectangles, not the counts, not the frontier, not the refusals, not the
34	 * receipt and not the phase. It has to be that way round rather than as a matter
35	 * of taste: the line is never written to a recording, so anything it could move
36	 * would be something a replay of the same run could not reproduce, and a
37	 * recording is the real stream line for line.
38	 */
39	
40	import { absence } from "../world/absence";
41	import type { WorldSummary } from "../world/apiSource";
42	import { toWorldView } from "../world/apiSource";
43	import { toClaim, toLink } from "../world/fromTheServer";
44	import { inFewWords, NOT_ON_THIS_MAP } from "../world/naming";
45	import type { Absence, ClaimView, LinkView, WorldView } from "../world/types";
46	import type {
47	  Activity,
48	  ActivityKind,
49	  Done,
50	  GenerationStarted,
51	  Link,
52	  ProposalAccepted,
53	  Proposition,
54	  PropositionId,
55	  ReadEvent,
56	  Receipt,
57	  Verdict,
58	} from "./events";
59	
60	/** One proposal the rules refused, as the strip beside the map lists it. */
61	export interface Refusal {
62	  /** Its place in the transcript, counting from 0. The engine's number. */
63	  readonly at: number;
64	  /** What the model wrote. Quoted, never drawn as a tile, never given an identifier. */
65	  readonly claimInWords: string;
66	  /** The validator's own sentences, one per rule broken, in the order it gave them. */
67	  readonly reasons: readonly string[];
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * One kind of line the reader could not act on, and how often it arrived.
72	 *
73	 * It is counted rather than dropped because a browser that swallows a line
74	 * makes a missing feature look like a working one — and it is counted **as one
75	 * of two kinds**, because *we have no name for this* and *we know that name and
76	 * could not read what came with it* are different facts about the map on
77	 * screen.
78	 */
79	export interface UnreadLine {
80	  /** How many arrived under this name. */
81	  readonly howMany: number;
82	  /** True when the name was one of the eight and its payload could not be read. */
83	  readonly unreadable: boolean;
84	}
85	
86	/**
87	 * One line about what the model is doing inside a call that has not come back.
88	 *
89	 * It is the `activity` event's three fields, kept as they arrived. Nothing here
90	 * is composed, shortened or translated: the strip does the shortening when it
91	 * draws, and what is kept is what the model said.
92	 */
93	export interface ActivityLine {
94	  /**
95	   * The open claim the call is working on, or null when the call is about no one
96	   * claim. It is what says which lines a proposal's arrival makes stale.
97	   */
98	  readonly about: PropositionId | null;
99	  /** Which of the three things the model was doing. */
100	  readonly kind: ActivityKind;
101	  /** The model's own words, verbatim. */
102	  readonly text: string;
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * The most the strip may say about what the model is doing right now: two lines.
107	 *
108	 * **Latest only, never a list.** The server sends at most about one of these a
109	 * second per call and the newest wins, so a browser that kept them all would
110	 * grow a log at the foot of the screen that nobody could read and that would
111	 * push the map up the page every second.
112	 *
113	 * **Two, because they are two different things.** A search is about the world —
114	 * a query issued, a page found — and is checkable. A thought is about the
115	 * model's own mind. Neither replaces the other, and the one about the mind says
116	 * whose mind it is, every time it is drawn.
117	 */
118	export interface WhatTheModelIsDoing {
119	  /** The latest `searching` or `found` line. They are one slot: found answers searching. */
120	  readonly searching: ActivityLine | null;
121	  /** The latest `thinking` line. */
122	  readonly thinking: ActivityLine | null;
123	}
124	
125	/** Nothing is being said about what the model is doing. Where every run starts and ends. */
126	export const SAYING_NOTHING: WhatTheModelIsDoing = { searching: null, thinking: null };
127	
128	/** One reserved rectangle at the growing edge of the map. Never a claim. */
129	export interface Skeleton {
130	  /** `skeleton:<claim id>`, or `skeleton:hypothesis` for the first one. A box's name. */
131	  readonly id: string;
132	  /** The one line it carries. The reader's own sentence, or the open claim's words. */
133	  readonly words: string;
134	  /** The open claim this one hangs off. Null for the first. */
135	  readonly after: PropositionId | null;
136	}
137	
138	/**
139	 * Where a generation is. Each is a different thing on screen, and none is a
140	 * spinner.
141	 *
142	 * - `waiting` — the request has gone and the first event has not come back.
143	 * - `growing` — proposals are arriving.
144	 * - `settled` — the last line closed properly and the map is finished.
145	 * - `stopped` — a cap ended the run. The map is finished too, and the strip says
146	 *   which cap, in the engine's own words for it.
147	 * - `failed` — something on our side broke. The map that was built stays exactly
148	 *   where it is.
149	 * - `ended_early` — the stream stopped without saying anything at all. Not a
150	 *   failure, because nothing failed that anybody can name: a server was
151	 *   restarted, a proxy gave up on an idle connection, a laptop went to sleep in
152	 *   the middle of a ten-minute run.
153	 */
154	export type Phase = "waiting" | "growing" | "settled" | "stopped" | "failed" | "ended_early";
155	
156	/**
157	 * Has the run stopped, whatever stopped it?
158	 *
159	 * Four of the five phases are over and one is not, and every screen that asks
160	 * asks the same question — so it is asked in one place. A screen listing the
161	 * four by hand is a screen that will list three of them the day a fifth way to
162	 * stop is added, and then a map will grow for ever in exactly one case.
163	 */
164	export function hasStopped(phase: Phase): boolean {
165	  return phase !== "waiting" && phase !== "growing";
166	}
167	
168	/** Everything the screen knows about a generation. */
169	export interface Growth {
170	  readonly phase: Phase;
171	  /** The engine's name for this run. Null until the run has started. */
172	  readonly generationId: string | null;
173	  /**
174	   * The seed every likelihood in this run was worked out from, exactly as the
175	   * engine wrote it — its digits, not a number.
176	   *
177	   * A seed can be nineteen digits long and JavaScript holds a whole number
178	   * exactly only up to sixteen, so the parsed value is already rounded. Nothing
179	   * here computes with a seed; it is printed under the map so a reader can ask
180	   * for the same one again, and what is printed is what came off the wire.
181	   * Null until the run has started; never worked out here.
182	   */
183	  readonly seed: string | null;
184	  /** The sentence the reader typed, as the run's first event repeated it back. */
185	  readonly hypothesis: string;
186	  /** The destination the reader named, or null on the Explore door. */
187	  readonly target: string | null;
188	  /**
189	   * The map as far as it has been built, in the same view model the canvas
190	   * already draws. Every number slot the engine has not spoken about reads its
191	   * absence, so a half-built map is drawn by the components that already exist,
192	   * unchanged.
193	   */
194	  readonly world: WorldView;
195	  /**
196	   * One per claim still open to expand. Rebuilt from the frontier on **either**
197	   * growth event — accepted or refused — and emptied when the likelihoods arrive,
198	   * where the frontier is empty by definition.
199	   */
200	  readonly skeletons: readonly Skeleton[];
201	  /** Every refusal, in the order they happened. Never trimmed, never summarised away. */
202	  readonly refusals: readonly Refusal[];
203	  /** The Verify door's answer, when a destination was named. */
204	  readonly verdict: Verdict | null;
205	  /** What the run cost. Null until the receipt arrives; never estimated meanwhile. */
206	  readonly receipt: Receipt | null;
207	  /** Why the generation stopped. Null until it does. */
208	  readonly done: Done | null;
209	  /** The one sentence a broken run left. Null otherwise. */
210	  readonly failure: string | null;
211	  /**
212	   * Arrows whose two ends are not both on the map yet, held rather than drawn.
213	   *
214	   * Expected to stay empty — the engine sends a claim and its incoming arrows in
215	   * one event — and kept because a wire with one end nowhere is a picture of a
216	   * thing that is not true.
217	   */
218	  readonly waitingWires: readonly Link[];
219	  /**
220	   * Every line the reader could not act on, and how many of each arrived.
221	   *
222	   * Two kinds, kept apart because they say different things to a reader. A name
223	   * this build has never heard of is a server that has learned a word, and the
224	   * map drawn from the rest is a correct map. A name this build knows whose
225	   * payload could not be read is a broken line, and the map may be missing what
226	   * that line carried.
227	   */
228	  readonly unknown: ReadonlyMap<string, UnreadLine>;
229	  /**
230	   * What the model is doing right now, and the **only** thing an `activity`
231	   * event changes.
232	   *
233	   * It touches nothing else here — not the map, not the rectangles, not the
234	   * refusals, not the receipt, not the phase — because a line that is never
235	   * recorded must never be able to move something a recording would have to
236	   * reproduce. Everything above is folded from the eight events a recording
237	   * holds, and folding the same recording twice gives the same map; this field
238	   * is folded from the one event a recording never holds, and it is empty on
239	   * every replay for that reason.
240	   *
241	   * **Who decides it is shown is the screen, not this.** A fold has not been
242	   * told whether the run it is folding is live or a recording being played back,
243	   * and it does not need to be: the screen knows, and it passes the strip
244	   * nothing on a replay — the same difference the seconds counter already makes.
245	   */
246	  readonly activity: WhatTheModelIsDoing;
247	}
248	
249	/**
250	 * What stands where a likelihood would go while a map is still being built.
251	 *
252	 * It is the vocabulary's third row — *nothing has been computed* — because that
253	 * is exactly what is true: the map is not finished, and every likelihood is
254	 * worked through the finished map at once, when it is finished.
255	 */
256	export const WHILE_IT_GROWS: Absence = absence(
257	  "no_engine",
258	  "The map is still being built. Every likelihood is worked through the whole map at once, " +
259	    "when the map is finished — a number worked out from half a map would be the answer to a " +
260	    "question about a map that will not exist in a second.",
261	);
262	
263	/**
264	 * The one sentence *Run details* carries while a map is still being built.
265	 *
266	 * **It does not say that anything has arrived**, because for the first
267	 * twenty-odd seconds of a run nothing has. The line this replaced read *"Every
268	 * claim and arrow on this map arrived from /api/generate…"* and it was written
269	 * from the run's first event onward — that is, over an empty map, asserting
270	 * arrivals that had not happened. What is true from the first event is where
271	 * the map is being built and how: nothing on it is typed in, and no likelihood
272	 * has been worked out yet.
273	 *
274	 * The route, the run's own name and the seed are printed beside it as three
275	 * readings rather than folded into the prose, so a reader can copy one.
276	 */
277	export const NOTHING_HERE_WAS_TYPED_IN =
278	  "Nothing on this map is typed in: every claim and every arrow on it was proposed by the model " +
279	  "and accepted by the map's own rules.";
280	
281	/**
282	 * The second sentence *Run details* carries, and only until the numbers land.
283	 *
284	 * It is true while the map is being built and false the moment the engine's
285	 * world arrives, so it is printed for exactly that long.
286	 */
287	export const NO_LIKELIHOOD_YET =
288	  "No likelihood has been worked out yet: the engine works them through the whole map at once, " +
289	  "when the map is finished.";
290	
291	/** An empty map, in the shape the canvas draws, with the reader's sentence as its title. */
292	function nothingYet(hypothesis: string): WorldView {
293	  return {
294	    // Until the run has a name of its own there is nothing to call this map. The
295	    // moment it has one, the name is the engine's.
296	    baseId: "",
297	    title: hypothesis,
298	    // The day the map is set on is the engine's day zero, and it arrives with the
299	    // world. Nothing on a growing map reads it — it is what an edit would be
300	    // dated by, and a map that is still being built cannot be edited.
301	    today: "",
302	    hypothesisId: "",
303	    claims: [],
304	    links: [],
305	    // Where this map came from is read in *Run details*, in the panel, from the
306	    // run's own name and seed. The map itself has no origin sentence of its own
307	    // until the engine hands one over with the likelihoods.
308	    origin: `${NOTHING_HERE_WAS_TYPED_IN} ${NO_LIKELIHOOD_YET}`,
309	  };
310	}
311	
312	/**
313	 * Where a generation starts: a request has gone and nothing has come back.
314	 *
315	 * @param hypothesis The sentence the reader typed, so the screen has something
316	 *   to put on the first reserved rectangle before the engine has said anything.
317	 * @param target The destination they named, or nothing on the Explore door.
318	 */
319	export function waitingFor(hypothesis: string, target: string | null = null): Growth {
320	  return {
321	    phase: "waiting",
322	    generationId: null,
323	    seed: null,
324	    hypothesis,
325	    target,
326	    world: nothingYet(hypothesis),
327	    skeletons: [],
328	    refusals: [],
329	    verdict: null,
330	    receipt: null,
331	    done: null,
332	    failure: null,
333	    waitingWires: [],
334	    unknown: new Map<string, UnreadLine>(),
335	    activity: SAYING_NOTHING,
336	  };
337	}
338	
339	/** The name of the rectangle held open for the claim a reader's own sentence becomes. */
340	export const FIRST_RECTANGLE = "skeleton:hypothesis";
341	
342	/** The name of the rectangle held open at one claim's growing edge. */
343	export function rectangleFor(claimId: PropositionId): string {
344	  return `skeleton:${claimId}`;
345	}
346	
347	/**
348	 * The reserved rectangles the frontier asks for, in the frontier's own order.
349	 *
350	 * The rectangles on screen are the frontier, drawn. That is a fact the stream
351	 * states on every growth event, never a guess made here — which is the whole
352	 * reason both growth events carry it.
353	 *
354	 * @param frontier The claims still open to expand, as the event named them.
355	 * @param claims The claims on the map, so a rectangle can quote the one it hangs
356	 *   off.
357	 */
358	function rectanglesFor(
359	  frontier: readonly PropositionId[],
360	  claims: readonly ClaimView[],
361	): Skeleton[] {
362	  const words = new Map(claims.map((claim) => [claim.id, claim.claim]));
363	  return frontier.map((id) => ({
364	    id: rectangleFor(id),
365	    words: `one step on from "${inFewWords(words.get(id) ?? NOT_ON_THIS_MAP)}"`,
366	    after: id,
367	  }));
368	}
369	
370	/**
371	 * One claim from the stream, as the canvas draws it while the map is still
372	 * growing.
373	 *
374	 * The same reader every other claim on this canvas goes through, with one slot
375	 * written over: **the model's likelihood reads its absence.** The claim carries
376	 * the number the model stated for it, and printing that during the growing would
377	 * put a number on screen that nothing has worked through the map — and then
378	 * replace it, which is four numbers nobody computed by the time four causes have
379	 * arrived.
380	 */
381	function growingClaim(proposition: Proposition): ClaimView {
382	  const claim = toClaim(proposition);
383	  return {
384	    ...claim,
385	    beliefs: { ...claim.beliefs, model: { absence: WHILE_IT_GROWS } },
386	  };
387	}
388	
389	/**
390	 * Every arrow whose two ends are now both on the map, and every one still
391	 * waiting.
392	 *
393	 * @param held The arrows held back so far.
394	 * @param arriving The arrows this event brought.
395	 * @param claims Every claim on the map once this event has been folded in.
396	 */
397	function wiresThatCanBeDrawn(
398	  held: readonly Link[],
399	  arriving: readonly Link[],
400	  claims: readonly ClaimView[],
401	): { drawn: LinkView[]; waiting: Link[] } {
402	  const there = new Set(claims.map((claim) => claim.id));
403	  const drawn: LinkView[] = [];
404	  const waiting: Link[] = [];
405	  for (const link of [...held, ...arriving]) {
406	    if (there.has(link.source) && there.has(link.target)) {
407	      drawn.push(toLink(link));
408	    } else {
409	      waiting.push(link);
410	    }
411	  }
412	  return { drawn, waiting };
413	}
414	
415	/** Which claim the map starts from: the one the engine called the hypothesis. */
416	function hypothesisAmong(claims: readonly ClaimView[], sofar: string): string {
417	  if (sofar !== "") {
418	    return sofar;
419	  }
420	  return claims.find((claim) => claim.kind === "hypothesis")?.id ?? "";
421	}
422	
423	/**
424	 * The seed this run drew with, as its digits.
425	 *
426	 * The reader puts the digits on the event because JavaScript cannot hold a
427	 * nineteen-digit whole number exactly. A caller that handed the events over by
428	 * hand has no digits to give, and the parsed number is then the whole of what is
429	 * known.
430	 */
431	function seedOf(event: GenerationStarted): string {
432	  return event.seed_as_written ?? String(event.seed);
433	}
434	
435	/** The run has started: a name, a seed, and one rectangle carrying the reader's own words. */
436	function started(was: Growth, event: GenerationStarted): Growth {
437	  return {
438	    ...was,
439	    phase: "growing",
440	    generationId: event.generation_id,
441	    seed: seedOf(event),
442	    hypothesis: event.hypothesis,
443	    target: event.target,
444	    world: {
445	      ...was.world,
446	      // **The map has no identifier of its own until it is finished**, and the
447	      // generation's is not it: a generation is a run and a map is a thing it
448	      // built, and one run can hand its map to any number of later questions.
449	      // It arrives with `beliefs_propagated`, as the engine's own `base_id`.
450	      // Putting the run's name here would hand it to the insert route as *the
451	      // map the new claim is going onto*, which is a different thing that
452	      // happens to be a string of the same shape — and it would do it on
453	      // exactly the two screens where the map is half-built.
454	      title: event.hypothesis,
455	    },
456	    skeletons: [{ id: FIRST_RECTANGLE, words: event.hypothesis, after: null }],
457	  };
458	}
459	
460	/**
461	 * The two lines once this one has arrived. Latest wins, and only in its own slot.
462	 *
463	 * @param lines What was being said before.
464	 * @param event The line that just arrived.
465	 */
466	function theLatest(lines: WhatTheModelIsDoing, event: Activity): WhatTheModelIsDoing {
467	  const line: ActivityLine = { about: event.about, kind: event.kind, text: event.text };
468	  return event.kind === "thinking" ? { ...lines, thinking: line } : { ...lines, searching: line };
469	}
470	
471	/**
472	 * Which calls a proposal that has just arrived is the answer to.
473	 *
474	 * A call is working on one open claim — the claim the proposal hangs off — and
475	 * an accepted proposal names that claim, as the source of the arrows it brought.
476	 * A proposal that hangs off nothing at all is the **opening** call coming back:
477	 * the one that turns the reader's own sentence into the first claim, and the one
478	 * whose activity lines are about no claim.
479	 *
480	 * @param event The accepted proposal.
481	 * @returns The claims whose calls this answers, with null standing for the
482	 *   opening call.
483	 */
484	function theCallsAnsweredBy(event: ProposalAccepted): ReadonlySet<PropositionId | null> {
485	  const answered = new Set<PropositionId | null>(event.links.map((link) => link.source));
486	  if (event.links.length === 0) {
487	    answered.add(null);
488	  }
489	  return answered;
490	}
491	
492	/**
493	 * The lines left once those calls have been answered.
494	 *
495	 * A line says what the model is doing *while a call is out*. When the call comes
496	 * back, the line is no longer true, and a strip still saying *searching the web*
497	 * under a sentence announcing what arrived is the browser asserting something
498	 * that has stopped being the case.
499	 *
500	 * @param lines What was being said.
501	 * @param answered The calls that have just come back.
502	 */
503	function withoutTheCalls(
504	  lines: WhatTheModelIsDoing,
505	  answered: ReadonlySet<PropositionId | null>,
506	): WhatTheModelIsDoing {
507	  const kept = (line: ActivityLine | null) =>
508	    line === null || answered.has(line.about) ? null : line;
509	  return { searching: kept(lines.searching), thinking: kept(lines.thinking) };
510	}
511	
512	/**
513	 * Fold one event into what the screen knows.
514	 *
515	 * @param was Everything known before this event.
516	 * @param event The event, with its name already joined onto its payload.
517	 * @returns Everything known after it, as a new object. Every one of the eight
518	 *   events changes something the map is made of — even an unknown name, which
519	 *   changes the count of how many of it arrived. **The ninth is the exception,
520	 *   and it is the exception on purpose:** an `activity` line changes only
521	 *   `activity`, and one that reaches a run which has already stopped changes
522	 *   nothing at all and hands the same object back. So a screen that wants to
523	 *   know whether something *arrived* asks `onlyTheStripChanged`, below, rather
524	 *   than comparing the two objects.
525	 */
526	export function fold(was: Growth, event: ReadEvent): Growth {
527	  switch (event.event) {
528	    case "generation_started":
529	      return started(was, event);
530	
531	    case "proposal_accepted": {
532	      const claims =
533	        event.proposition === null
534	          ? was.world.claims
535	          : [...was.world.claims, growingClaim(event.proposition)];
536	      const { drawn, waiting } = wiresThatCanBeDrawn(was.waitingWires, event.links, claims);
537	      return {
538	        ...was,
539	        phase: "growing",
540	        world: {
541	          ...was.world,
542	          hypothesisId: hypothesisAmong(claims, was.world.hypothesisId),
543	          claims,
544	          // The arrows already on the map, and every one that can now be drawn:
545	          // the ones this event brought, and any that were held back waiting for
546	          // their second end. A held arrow was never on the map, so nothing is
547	          // drawn twice.
548	          links: [...was.world.links, ...drawn],
549	        },
550	        skeletons: rectanglesFor(event.frontier, claims),
551	        waitingWires: waiting,
552	        // The call this proposal came from has come back, so whatever it was
553	        // last seen doing is over. A call still out, on another claim, keeps
554	        // saying what it is doing.
555	        activity: withoutTheCalls(was.activity, theCallsAnsweredBy(event)),
556	      };
557	    }
558	
559	    case "proposal_rejected":
560	      return {
561	        ...was,
562	        phase: "growing",
563	        // **A refusal clears both lines, where an acceptance clears only the
564	        // ones it answers.** A refusal carries no claim it hangs off — what it
565	        // carries is the model's words and the rules it broke — so the browser
566	        // cannot say which call came back, and the honest answer to *which of
567	        // these is still true* is *we no longer know*. A line that is still true
568	        // is back within about a second; a line that is false stays false.
569	        activity: SAYING_NOTHING,
570	        refusals: [
571	          ...was.refusals,
572	          {
573	            at: event.at,
574	            claimInWords: event.claim_in_words,
575	            // The validator's own sentences, one per rule broken, with nothing
576	            // added and nothing dropped. The rule's code is never drawn.
577	            reasons: event.violations.map((violation) => violation.message),
578	          },
579	        ],
580	        // The same field the accepted event carries. A claim closed by its third
581	        // refusal in a row is gone from it here, so its rectangle comes down on
582	        // the refusal rather than waiting for a proposal that may never come.
583	        skeletons: rectanglesFor(event.frontier, was.world.claims),
584	      };
585	
586	    case "beliefs_propagated": {
587	      const summary: WorldSummary = {
588	        id: event.world.base_id,
589	        title: was.hypothesis,
590	        day: event.world.day_zero,
591	        // The seed the run reported, not the one on the world: both are the
592	        // same seed, and only the first was read as its digits.
593	        origin: originOfTheFinishedMap(
594	          was,
595	          was.seed ?? String(event.world.seed),
596	          event.world.versions,
597	        ),
598	      };
599	      return {
600	        ...was,
601	        // The engine's world **is** the world. Whatever was drawn while it grew
602	        // is thrown away rather than merged into: two versions of one map
603	        // eventually disagree, and then nobody can say which is right.
604	        world: toWorldView(event.world, summary),
605	        // The frontier is empty by definition once the map is finished, so there
606	        // is nothing left for a reserved rectangle to stand for.
607	        skeletons: [],
608	        waitingWires: [],
609	      };
610	    }
611	
612	    case "verdict":
613	      return { ...was, verdict: event };
614	
615	    case "receipt":
616	      return { ...was, receipt: event };
617	
618	    case "done":
619	      return {
620	        ...was,
621	        done: event,
622	        phase: event.reason === "reached_terminal" ? "settled" : "stopped",
623	        // Nothing is out, so nothing is being done. The lines go with the
624	        // seconds, and for the same reason: both measure a wait that is over.
625	        activity: SAYING_NOTHING,
626	      };
627	
628	    case "failed":
629	      // The map that had been built stays exactly where it is. Nothing is
630	      // cleared and nothing is greyed: a reader whose run broke after twenty
631	      // claims keeps the twenty claims.
632	      //
633	      // **The rectangles go, and only the rectangles.** A reserved rectangle is
634	      // a promise that a claim is coming, and after this nothing is: the chapter
635	      // says no rectangle may ever stand where nothing will arrive, and a broken
636	      // run is the case it does not name. The claims still open are in the
637	      // working either way, so nothing is lost by taking the boxes down — what
638	      // would be lost by leaving them is a reader waiting for a claim for ever.
639	      return {
640	        ...was,
641	        phase: "failed",
642	        failure: event.message,
643	        skeletons: [],
644	        activity: SAYING_NOTHING,
645	      };
646	
647	    case "activity":
648	      // **The one event that changes only what the strip may say.** Not the
649	      // map, not the rectangles, not the counts, not the frontier, not the
650	      // receipt and not the phase — a run that has not started does not start
651	      // because the model said something, and a run that has stopped stays
652	      // stopped and says nothing more about what is being done.
653	      return hasStopped(was.phase) ? was : { ...was, activity: theLatest(was.activity, event) };
654	
655	    case "unknown": {
656	      const counted = new Map(was.unknown);
657	      const before = counted.get(event.name);
658	      counted.set(event.name, {
659	        howMany: (before?.howMany ?? 0) + 1,
660	        // Once a name has arrived unreadable it stays marked so: a name that
661	        // came through twice, once broken, is a name that broke.
662	        unreadable: (before?.unreadable ?? false) || event.unreadable === true,
663	      });
664	      return { ...was, unknown: counted };
665	    }
666	  }
667	}
668	
669	/** The one sentence under a finished map, saying where every number on it came from. */
670	function originOfTheFinishedMap(was: Growth, seed: string, versions: number): string {
671	  const spelled = versions.toLocaleString("en-GB").replace(/,/g, " ");
672	  return (
673	    `Every claim and arrow on this map was proposed at /api/generate and accepted by the map's ` +
674	    `own rules; every likelihood was worked out by the engine from that map, at seed ${seed}, ` +
675	    `over ${spelled} versions of the map. The working is generation ` +
676	    `${was.generationId ?? "this run"}, and the same sentence and seed give the same map again.`
677	  );
678	}
679	
680	/** Fold a whole stream, in order. What a test builds a finished map with. */
681	export function foldAll(from: Growth, events: readonly ReadEvent[]): Growth {
682	  return events.reduce(fold, from);
683	}
684	
685	/**
686	 * Did the last event change only what the strip may say, and nothing else?
687	 *
688	 * **This is what keeps the seconds counter honest.** The reading at the foot of
689	 * a map says *nothing new on the map for N s*, and it starts again every time
690	 * something arrives. An `activity` line is not an arrival in that sense: it is
691	 * the model saying what it is doing inside a call that has not come back, and a
692	 * counter that started again on every one of them would read *nothing new on the
693	 * map for 1 s* for three solid minutes while nothing whatever reached the map —
694	 * which is exactly the screen that looks busy while nothing happens, the thing
695	 * the counter was built to stop. So the counter measures arrivals on the map,
696	 * its words say so, and the lines say the tool is alive in their own right, by
697	 * changing in front of the reader every few seconds.
698	 *
699	 * It compares every other field by identity rather than by value, which is what
700	 * `fold` gives it: every branch above hands back the same objects for the fields
701	 * it did not touch.
702	 *
703	 * @param was What was known before the event, or null before anything at all.
704	 * @param now What is known after it.
705	 */
706	export function onlyTheStripChanged(was: Growth | null, now: Growth): boolean {
707	  if (was === null) {
708	    return false;
709	  }
710	  const { activity: _wasSaying, ...before } = was;
711	  const { activity: _nowSaying, ...after } = now;
712	  return (Object.keys(before) as (keyof typeof before)[]).every(
713	    (field) => before[field] === after[field],
714	  );
715	}
716	
717	/**
718	 * The body ended, and nothing on it said the run was over.
719	 *
720	 * **A dropped stream is a finished generation with no terminator**
721	 * (`spec/generation/streaming.md`). Every stream a reader stayed for ends in
722	 * exactly one `done` or one `failed`; a stream that ends without either did not
723	 * *fail*, it simply stopped being delivered — a server restarted, a proxy gave
724	 * up on a connection it thought was idle, a laptop slept in the middle of a
725	 * ten-minute run. None of those is a fault anybody can name, and calling it one
726	 * would put a sentence on screen blaming something that may be blameless.
727	 *
728	 * **The rectangles come down.** They are the other half of the chapter's rule
729	 * that no rectangle ever stands where nothing is coming: after this, nothing is.
730	 * A map left growing for ever is the one screen in this product that lies
731	 * without saying anything — it is drawn exactly as a map that is about to change
732	 * and it is never going to change again.
733	 *
734	 * **The map is kept.** Everything that arrived is what arrived, and the working
735	 * as far as it got is still readable at the transcript route.
736	 *
737	 * It is not a wire event and is never folded as one. The server did not say
738	 * this; the reader noticed it, by reaching the end of a body.
739	 *
740	 * @param was Everything known when the body ended.
741	 * @returns The same state when a terminator had already arrived — a body that
742	 *   ends after `done` is a body ending normally — and an ended-early one when
743	 *   none had.
744	 */
745	export function theStreamEnded(was: Growth): Growth {
746	  if (hasStopped(was.phase)) {
747	    return was;
748	  }
749	  // And what the model was last seen doing goes with them, for the same reason:
750	  // nothing is out, so nothing is being done.
751	  return { ...was, phase: "ended_early", skeletons: [], activity: SAYING_NOTHING };
752	}

"""Find the one scripted intervention a recording can answer, or nothing at all.

    Matched on the exact words after trimming surrounding spaces — the same rule
    that picks which recording plays, because one matching rule is easier to trust
    than two. There is no fuzzy matching and there will not be: drafting a claim
    from a sentence is the model's job, and a similarity score doing it badly
    would be a piece of state nobody could trace to an input, a rule or a source.
    """
    wanted = claim_in_words.strip()
    for recording in replay.every_recording():
        if recording.header.insert.claim_in_words.strip() == wanted:
            drafted = recording.header.insert.answer
            return drafted
    return None


def _no_such_map(base_id: str) -> str:
    """Say that no map answers to that name, and say what a caller should send.

    The commonest wrong answer is a *generation's* identifier: a run and the map
    it built are two different things, and one run's map outlives the question
    that made it. So the sentence names both, rather than leaving somebody to
    guess which of two identifiers they are holding.
    """
    return (
        f"{engine.no_such_example(base_id)} If you are holding a map this program "
        "generated, send the map's own identifier — the one a world carries as its "
        "`base_id` — and not the identifier of the generation that built it."
    )


def _today() -> date:
    """The day this run is happening, read once and passed down.

    The one clock in the pipeline. Everything below takes the day as an argument,
    which is what lets a recorded run and a live one be compared at all.
    """
    return datetime.now(tz=UTC).date()


def _what_it_would_break(onto: Graph, drafted: Insert) -> tuple[Violation, ...]:
    """Check a drafted claim against the map it is going onto, exactly like any other.

    The same `validate`, the same codes, the same sentences a refused proposal
    gets — because a claim a person asked for is not held to a lower standard than
    one the model offered. Only what the edit **introduced** counts, for the same
    reason it does when a proposal is judged: a map already missing something
    would refuse every edit until the last one.

    Args:
        onto: The map the new claim is going onto.
        drafted: The claim and its arrows.

    Returns:
        Every reason it does not fit, or nothing at all.
    """
    folded = apply(
        onto, Branch(id="drafting", label="a claim somebody asked for", interventions=(drafted,))
    )
    if isinstance(folded, list):
        return tuple(folded)
    already = set(validate(onto))

"""The three routes that work a branch through a map and say what it did.

The point of these tests is the crossing. A world leaves the program as JSON —
eight claims, a likelihood and a range each, a likelihood for every day of the
window and a named word beside it — and has to arrive as the same world. A
refused branch has to arrive as a list of sentences and a status that says whose
fault it was, never as a stack trace.

These run at a **small budget** unless the test is about the budget itself: the
shipped run is two thousand versions of the map times eight worlds each, and a
difference costs four runs of the engine. Nothing about what the routes answer
changes with the budget, only how steady the numbers are.
"""

from typing import Any

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from hypothesis import HealthCheck, given, settings
from hypothesis import strategies as st

from katalyst.api.main import app
from katalyst.domain import Belief, Diff, World, diff
from katalyst.engine import worlds as engine
from katalyst.fixtures import HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE
from tests.strategies import branches, graphs

SEED = 20261001
"""The seed the worked example's demo uses, so a test and a screenshot agree."""

SMALL: dict[str, int] = {"versions": 16, "worlds": 4}
"""Sixty-four draws rather than sixteen thousand. See this file's own note."""

STRIKE: dict[str, Any] = HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE.model_dump(mode="json")
"""The shipped branch as the browser would send it: a whole branch, not a name."""

no_wandering = settings(
    max_examples=15,
    deadline=None,
    suppress_health_check=[HealthCheck.function_scoped_fixture, HealthCheck.too_slow],
)


def _asked(client: TestClient, route: str, **body: Any) -> Any:
    """Ask one route a question and give back its answer, whatever the status."""
    return client.post(f"/api/{route}", json={"base_id": "hormuz", "seed": SEED, **SMALL, **body})


def test_a_base_world_answers_with_every_claim_on_the_map() -> None:
    """Asking with no branch gives the map as it stands, with a number for every claim.

    That is what the browser asks for first. The route that hands out the stored
    examples still hands out a map and its branches and nothing computed, because
    a map is written by hand and a world never is — so the world arrives here, from
    the engine, rather than being typed into the example.
    """
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        answer = _asked(client, "worlds")

    assert answer.status_code == 200
    world = World.model_validate(answer.json())
    assert world.branch_id is None
    assert world.base_id == "hormuz"
    assert {one.id for one in world.graph.propositions} == set(world.beliefs)
    for claim_id, belief in world.beliefs.items():
        assert 0.0 <= belief.lo <= belief.p <= belief.hi <= 1.0, claim_id
        assert belief.owner == "model"
    assert world.conditionals == {}, "a freshly built world holds no arrow numbers"


def test_the_strike_branch_answers_with_a_world_that_names_its_branch() -> None:
    """A branch sent whole comes back worked through, saying which branch it was.

    The branch travels in the request because there is nowhere to keep one yet.
    Which branch a world came from is written in by the layer that knows, because
    working the numbers through takes a map and the values its edits fixed and
    never the branch itself.
    """
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        answer = _asked(client, "worlds", branch=STRIKE)

"""The three routes a generation is asked for, watched and read back through.

Every test here runs with **no key**, which is the point: the recording is written
into a throwaway directory from the fake answers the pipeline's own tests use, so
the whole stream — its grammar, its terminator, its refusals, its receipt — is
provable today without a model, a network or a penny.

**The request says how a run starts**, and these tests say it too. `stream` asks
for the default, which is a recording; `live_stream` asks for a live run, and the
tests that use it hand the seam a script instead of a model. A test that wants a
live run therefore says so rather than relying on a key being configured — which
is what the route used to read and deliberately no longer does (record 0012,
amended 2026-09-21).
"""

import json
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from katalyst.api import generate
from katalyst.api.main import app
from katalyst.engine import replay
from katalyst.engine.grow import grow
from katalyst.engine.outcome import Caps

def test_a_world_needs_no_key_of_any_kind() -> None:
    """Nothing here asks a language model anything, so nothing here needs a key.

    The whole engine is arithmetic over a map somebody wrote down. A route that
    quietly needed a key would make the tests need one too, and the checks that run
    on every change are given none.
    """
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        answer = _asked(client, "worlds", branch=STRIKE)

    assert answer.status_code == 200

class Graph(BaseModel):
    """A whole cause-and-effect map: claims, the arrows between them, and which claim started it.

    A graph is immutable. Nothing edits one in place — a change is an intervention
    recorded on a branch, and applying a branch produces a new graph. A graph is a
    proposal until the validity rules have returned an empty list for it; nothing
    reaches the canvas before that.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    # Open question 2 in spec/graph/validity.md: claims, arrows and branches each
    # have a named identifier type, and a map does not. Add `GraphId`, or leave
    # this a plain string?
    id: str = Field(description="Minted by our code, never by the model.")
    propositions: tuple[Proposition, ...] = Field(
        description=(
            "Every claim on the map, in no particular order. A tuple, so it cannot be appended to."
        )
    )
    links: tuple[Link, ...] = Field(
        description=(
            "Every arrow on the map. Each names a source and a target that must be present above."
        )
    )
    hypothesis_id: PropositionId = Field(
        description=(
            "The claim the user started from. Must name a proposition present in `propositions` — "
            "that much is checked when the object is built. That the named claim is actually of "
            "kind 'hypothesis', and that no second one exists, is checked by the validity rules."
        )
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _hypothesis_is_on_the_map(self) -> "Graph":
        """Check that the claim the map started from is one of the claims on it.

        A map pointing at a claim that does not exist cannot be drawn, cannot be
        diffed and cannot be explained, and no model proposal produces one — our
        own code assembles this object, so a mismatch is our bug.

        Returns:
            This same graph, once the starting claim has been found.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no proposition on the map carries that identifier.

@given(st.data())
@no_wandering
def test_a_branch_written_for_another_map_is_answered_or_refused_and_never_breaks(
    data: st.DataObject,
) -> None:
    """Send a branch built for a different map and the answer is a world or a refusal.

    Never a server error. The subjects of a branch drawn against some other map
    usually name nothing on this one, so most of these are refused — but a few land
    on a claim that happens to share a name, and those are answered like any other.
    """
    elsewhere = data.draw(graphs())
    branch = data.draw(branches(elsewhere))

    with TestClient(app) as client:
        answer = _asked(client, "worlds", branch=branch.model_dump(mode="json"))

    assert answer.status_code in {200, 422}, answer.text
    if answer.status_code == 422:
        for one in answer.json()["detail"]:
            assert one["code"] and one["subject"] is not None and one["message"]


def test_asking_for_an_example_that_does_not_exist_answers_in_words() -> None:
    """An unknown example name is a 404 with a sentence naming the ones that do exist."""
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        answers = [
            _asked(client, "worlds", base_id="photonics"),
            _asked(client, "worlds/diff", base_id="photonics", branch_b=STRIKE),
            _asked(client, "worlds/conditional", base_id="photonics", link_id="H->B"),
        ]

    for answer in answers:
        assert answer.status_code == 404
        message = answer.json()["detail"]
        assert "photonics" in message
        assert "hormuz" in message
        assert len(message.split()) >= 8


def test_a_world_needs_no_key_of_any_kind() -> None:
    """Nothing here asks a language model anything, so nothing here needs a key.

    The whole engine is arithmetic over a map somebody wrote down. A route that
    quietly needed a key would make the tests need one too, and the checks that run
    on every change are given none.
    """
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        answer = _asked(client, "worlds", branch=STRIKE)

    assert answer.status_code == 200
    assert "key" not in answer.text.lower()

@pytest.fixture
def a_generation_this_process_is_holding() -> Iterator[str]:
    """Fold one stand-in generation into this process and give back its map's own name.

    A finished generation is kept in memory, under the identifier of the map it
    built, for the life of the process — which is what lets a reviewer who has just
    watched a map draw itself suppose something on it. Nothing here calls a model:
    what stands in for the generated map is the stored one under a minted name,
    which is exactly what a generated map is to every route below — a map that
    answers to no stored name.

    Yields:
        The map's own identifier, which is what a request sends as its `base_id`.
    """
    held.forget_everything()
    held.remember(
        Transcript(
            generation_id="01JGENERATIONTHATBUILTIT0",
            hypothesis="The Strait of Hormuz is going to open next week.",
            seed=SEED,
            # The day the run happened, which is its map's day zero. The stored
            # example's own date is used so that the two worlds below differ by
            # the name of the map and by nothing else.
            on=FIXTURE_DATE,
            mode="replay",
        ),
        HORMUZ.model_copy(update={"id": A_GENERATED_MAP}),
        in_flight=False,
    )
    yield A_GENERATED_MAP
    held.forget_everything()


def test_a_world_is_built_on_a_generated_map_held_by_its_id(
    a_generation_this_process_is_holding: str,
) -> None:
    """A map this process generated answers here under its own name, like any stored one.

    This is the whole of what lets a reader edit a map they have just watched
    build itself: the six edits, a branch, the two worlds and the change list all
    go through these routes with the generated map's identifier as the base, and
    nothing about them knows or cares where the map came from.

    The proof is the comparison rather than any number written down here: the same
    map under a minted name gives the same world, to the byte, apart from the name
    itself.
    """
    generated = a_generation_this_process_is_holding
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        answer = _asked(client, "worlds", base_id=generated)
        stored = _asked(client, "worlds")

    assert answer.status_code == 200, answer.text
    world = World.model_validate(answer.json())
    assert world.base_id == generated
    assert world.branch_id is None
    assert {one.id for one in world.graph.propositions} == set(world.beliefs)
    for claim_id, belief in world.beliefs.items():
        assert 0.0 <= belief.lo <= belief.p <= belief.hi <= 1.0, claim_id
        assert belief.owner == "model"

    from_the_stored_one = World.model_validate(stored.json())
    assert world.beliefs == from_the_stored_one.beliefs
    assert world.series == from_the_stored_one.series
    assert world.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"base_id", "graph"}) == (
        from_the_stored_one.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"base_id", "graph"})
    )


def test_a_branch_folded_onto_a_generated_map_moves_the_same_endings(
    a_generation_this_process_is_holding: str,
) -> None:
    """Supposing something on a generated map gives two worlds and a ranked change list.

    The browser's *Change this claim* is this pair of requests and nothing else: a
    world with the branch folded on, and the difference between that world and the
    one before it. Both have to answer on a generated base, or the panel beside a
    map somebody just watched build itself has nothing to draw.
    """
    generated = a_generation_this_process_is_holding
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        after = _asked(client, "worlds", base_id=generated, branch=STRIKE)
        change = _asked(client, "worlds/diff", base_id=generated, branch_b=STRIKE)
        on_the_stored_one = _asked(client, "worlds/diff", branch_b=STRIKE)

    assert after.status_code == 200, after.text
    assert World.model_validate(after.json()).branch_id == HORMUZ_THEN_STRIKE.id

    assert change.status_code == 200, change.text
    difference = Diff.model_validate(change.json())
    assert difference.base_id == generated
    assert difference.claims["S"].state == "added"
    assert difference.rows, "an edit that reaches an ending has rows to show for it"
    assert [one.rank for one in difference.rows] == sorted(
        (one.rank for one in difference.rows), reverse=True
    )
    # The same edit on the same map under its stored name moves the same endings
    # in the same order, which is the one thing worth asserting about the numbers.
    also = Diff.model_validate(on_the_stored_one.json())
    assert [one.claim_id for one in difference.rows] == [one.claim_id for one in also.rows]
    assert difference.summary == also.summary


def test_a_generation_this_process_no_longer_holds_says_so() -> None:
    """A generated map is held for the life of the process, and the refusal says that.

    A restarted server has forgotten every map it generated, and a reader who
    refreshes on one then asks for a world under an identifier nothing answers to.
    Naming the stored examples alone would leave them thinking they had mistyped a

    with TestClient(app) as client:

    message = answer.json()["detail"]
    assert "01JGENERATEDMAPLONGGONE00" in message
    assert "hormuz" in message
    assert "life of the process" in message
    assert len(message.split()) >= 8

def no_such_example(base_id: str) -> str:
    """Say, in one sentence, that no map answers to this name — stored or generated.

    **Two different things can be true of a name that matches nothing**, and a
    reader told only the first will think they mistyped. The stored examples ship
    with the program and are always here. A map this program generated is held in
    memory under its own identifier for the life of the process that built it, so
    a map somebody watched build itself really is gone after a restart — and
    saying only "there is no stored example called this" would leave them hunting
    for a typing mistake in a name that was real ten minutes ago.

    Args:
        base_id: The name that was asked for.

    Returns:
        A sentence for the reader, never a code and never a stack trace.
    """
    offered = ", ".join(one.id for one in EXAMPLES)
    return (
        f"There is no map called '{base_id}' here. "
        f"The examples this program ships with are: {offered}. "
        "A map this program generated is held under its own identifier for the "
        "life of the process that built it, so one built before a restart is gone."
    )

cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04-edit-a-generated-map && git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
test(api): a world is built on a generated map held by its id

The route already does it: `example_named` falls through to the map this
process is holding, so `/api/worlds` with a generated map's own identifier
folds a branch onto it exactly as onto a stored example. Three tests say so
rather than leaving it to be discovered — one world, one branch and its
difference, and the sentence a reader gets when the process no longer holds
the map.

The refusal sentence was the one thing that was not true enough. "There is no
stored example called this" sends a reader who watched a map build itself
hunting for a typing mistake in a name that was real ten minutes ago; it now
says a generated map is held for the life of the process that built it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1
